title: Shapley-Folkman-Starr Theorem: Economic Context
content:
This file formalizes Starr's (1969) economic application of the Shapley-Folkman lemma. The key insight: even if individual agent preferences or feasible sets are non-convex, the *aggregate* market demand is 'approximately convex' in a quantitative sense.

**Historical setting**: Shapley and Folkman proved their lemma in 1967 unpublished correspondence (included as an appendix in Starr's 1969 *Econometrica* paper). Starr's contribution was recognizing the economic significance: the lemma gives a uniform bound on non-convexity that is *independent of the number of agents*, making large markets approximately competitive.

**Three main results**:
1. `convexHull_dist_le` — elementary distance lemma for convex hulls
2. `shapley_folkman_starr` — the main theorem: dist(x, ΣSᵢ) ≤ dim(E)·δ for x ∈ conv(ΣSᵢ)
3. `large_economy_near_convex` — corollary: per-agent error d·δ/n → 0 as n → ∞
mathContext: **Setup**: $E$ a finite-dimensional normed space, $\{S_i\}_{i \in t}$ sets with pairwise distances $\leq \delta$, $x \in \text{conv}(\sum_i S_i)$. **Main bound**: $\|x - x'\| \leq d \cdot \delta$ where $d = \dim(E)$ and $x' \in \sum_i S_i$.

title: convexHull_dist_le: Distance Bound via Convex Ball
content:
`convexHull_dist_le` proves: if $p \in \text{conv}(S)$ and every $s \in S$ satisfies $\text{dist}(s,q) \leq \delta$, then $\text{dist}(p,q) \leq \delta$.

**Proof idea**: The closed ball $B(q,\delta)$ is convex and contains $S$. By `convexHull_min` (the convex hull is the smallest convex set containing $S$), $\text{conv}(S) \subseteq B(q,\delta)$. Hence $p \in B(q,\delta)$, i.e., $\text{dist}(p,q) \leq \delta$.

`convexHull_dist_le_diam` is the diameter corollary: if every pair in $S$ has distance $\leq \delta$, and $q \in S$, then $p \in \text{conv}(S)$ satisfies $\text{dist}(p,q) \leq \delta$.
mathContext: $\text{conv}(S) \subseteq B(q,\delta)$ because: $S \subseteq B(q,\delta)$ (by hypothesis) and $B(q,\delta)$ is convex (proved via `convex_closedBall`). By minimality of convex hull (`convexHull_min`): $\text{conv}(S) \subseteq B(q,\delta)$.

title: shapley_folkman_starr: Main Economic Bound
content:
The main theorem formalizes Starr's 1969 result. Given $x \in \text{conv}(\sum_{i \in t} S_i)$ where each $S_i$ has diameter $\leq \delta$, there exists $x' \in \sum_{i \in t} S_i$ with $\text{dist}(x, x') \leq \dim(E) \cdot \delta$.

**Proof steps**:
1. Apply `sum_close_to_convexHull` (from parent) to get $f : \iota \to E$ with $f(i) \in \text{conv}(S_i)$ and $\sum f = x$, plus $J = \{i : f(i) \notin S_i\}$ with $|J| \leq \dim(E)$.
2. For each $j \in J$, choose any $g(j) \in S(j)$; for $i \notin J$, keep $g(i) = f(i) \in S(i)$.
3. $x' = \sum g \in \sum S_i$ (term-by-term membership).
4. `Finset.sum_subset` cancels all non-excess terms: $\sum(f - g) = \sum_{j \in J}(f(j) - g(j))$.
5. `norm_sum_le` + `convexHull_dist_le_diam` bounds each term by $\delta$.
6. Total: $\text{dist}(x,x') \leq |J| \cdot \delta \leq \dim(E) \cdot \delta$.
mathContext:
The key calculation:
$$\|x - x'\| = \|\textstyle\sum_{j \in J}(f_j - g_j)\| \leq \sum_{j \in J}\|f_j - g_j\| \leq |J| \cdot \delta \leq \dim(E) \cdot \delta$$
where $f_j \in \text{conv}(S_j)$, $g_j \in S_j$, and each $\|f_j - g_j\| \leq \delta$ by `convexHull_dist_le_diam` (using the diameter bound $\delta$ for $S_j$).

title: large_economy_near_convex: Vanishing Per-Agent Error
content:
The large economy corollary: for $n$ agents each with feasible set $S$ (diameter $\leq \delta$), any $x \in \text{conv}(n \cdot S)$ has $x' \in n \cdot S$ with $\text{dist}(x, x') \leq \dim(E) \cdot \delta$.

**Economic interpretation**: dividing by $n$, the *average* error is at most $\dim(E) \cdot \delta / n \to 0$. In a market with many agents, the convexified and actual aggregate demands are indistinguishable per capita.

**Proof**: Use $n \cdot S = \sum_{i \in \text{Fin}(n)} S$ (by `Finset.sum_const` + `Fintype.card_fin`) and apply `shapley_folkman_starr` with the constant family $S_i = S$.
mathContext: $n \cdot S = \sum_{i : \text{Fin}(n)} S_i$ where $S_i = S$ for all $i$. The Shapley-Folkman bound $d \cdot \delta$ is independent of $n$, so per-agent error $= d \cdot \delta / n \to 0$.

title: no_excess_for_convex: Convex Sets Contribute Zero Error
content:
`no_excess_for_convex` shows that if $S$ is convex then $\text{conv}(S) = S$, so any $x \in \text{conv}(S)$ already lies in $S$. This means convex summands $S_i$ never produce excess indices in the Shapley-Folkman decomposition — only non-convex summands contribute to the approximation error.

**Tightness**: The bound $d \cdot \delta$ is tight when all non-convexity is concentrated in $d$ summands (which can each contribute error $\delta$).
mathContext: $S$ convex $\Rightarrow$ $\text{conv}(S) = S$ (`Convex.convexHull_eq`). All error in the Shapley-Folkman bound comes from the $\leq d$ excess indices where $f(i) \in \text{conv}(S_i) \setminus S_i$ — impossible when $S_i$ is convex.
